solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Juvenile bully everyone must stop

indicators.note: to stop something is to plug it, so one word goes inside the other like a stopper

blocks.note: to cow someone is to bully or intimidate them
everyone is all

explanation.surface: A young thug is pushing others around and everybody has to put an end to it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Juvenile bully' reads as a single noun phrase, but juvenile is the definition and bully a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Callow describes someone young and inexperienced, which is what juvenile means as an adjective.

clue.text: Benefit claim Adam occasionally brought up, receiving very little

indicators.note: occasionally means now and then, so every other letter is kept
receiving takes something in, so another piece is placed inside
in a down answer, brought up means read from bottom to top

blocks.note: the even letters of claim Adam, run together
V is the abbreviation for very

explanation.surface: A welfare application for Adam keeps getting raised, but brings in almost nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Benefit claim' reads as one welfare phrase, but the definition stops at Benefit; 'very little' means just the abbreviation V.
explanation.definitionFit: Avail as a noun means use or advantage, as in to no avail, so it equals benefit.

clue.text: Listen in secret, not about to get discouraged

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other
about is c, from circa, and not means it is taken out

blocks.note: to hear is to listen
closet as an adjective means secret, as in a closet fan

explanation.surface: Eavesdropping without regard to anything leaves someone disheartened.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Listen in' looks like the phrase for eavesdropping, but the words split; about is C, the abbreviation of circa, which drops from CLOSET.
explanation.definitionFit: To lose heart is an idiom meaning to become dispirited and stop feeling hopeful.

clue.text: Carried on having regular paid employment

blocks.note: first meaning: conducted, as in to wage a war or campaign
second meaning: earning a salary or wages

explanation.surface: Someone continued in a steady salaried job.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb wage means conduct a campaign, and the adjective describes workers receiving a regular salary.

clue.text: Writer circles somewhat empty bar

indicators.note: to circle something is to go all the way round it, so one piece encloses another
an empty word has lost all its inside letters, keeping just the two ends

blocks.note: a Biro is a ballpoint pen, a common crossword writer
the first and last letters of somewhat

explanation.surface: An author walks around a bar that is fairly quiet.
explanation.walkthrough: BIRO is the British brand name for a ballpoint pen, standing in for any writer.
explanation.definitionFit: A bistro is a small informal restaurant serving drinks, close enough to a bar or café.

clue.text: Tower of London guide, non-vegan?

definitions.note: cryptic: a person who consumes beef

blocks.note: first meaning: a Yeoman Warder at the Tower of London
second meaning, read literally: someone who eats steak

explanation.surface: Is the ceremonial guide at the Tower a meat eater?
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the playful literal reading of the word as one who eats beef.
explanation.definitionFit: Beefeaters are the Yeoman Warders who guard the Tower of London and give guided tours to visitors.

clue.text: Sort of boom in flipping casinos, since banned

indicators.note: something banned is excluded, so those letters are taken out
flipping turns something over, so the letters run the other way

blocks.note: taken as written
as can mean since, as in as it was late

explanation.surface: A boom in gambling halls since they were outlawed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Since' looks like a time word in the surface, but it is a synonym taken out of the gambling halls before they are turned over.
explanation.definitionFit: A sonic boom is the loud bang made by an aircraft breaking the sound barrier.

clue.text: Minor star out in bad weather

indicators.note: out can mean wrong or disordered, so these letters must be rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written, for rearranging

explanation.surface: A lesser celebrity is outdoors in foul weather.
explanation.definitionFit: A rainstorm is a heavy downpour with wind, an example of bad weather.

clue.text: Marsupial that hurt round, minute mammal

indicators.note: turning round makes the cry face the other way, so it is read backwards

blocks.note: ow is what someone says when something hurts
M is the abbreviation for minute
the bat is a flying mammal

explanation.surface: A pouched animal felt pain after a round with a tiny mammal.
explanation.definitionFit: The wombat is a burrowing Australian marsupial with a pouch for its young.

clue.text: Island country, formerly one area overlooked

indicators.note: what is overlooked is left out, so those letters are dropped

blocks.note: the former name of Zimbabwe
I is the Roman numeral one
A is the abbreviation for area

explanation.surface: An island nation of old had a region ignored.
explanation.walkthrough: Take IA from the end of RHODESIA.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhodes is a Greek island in the Aegean, site of the ancient Colossus.

clue.text: Says yes to old gangsters right away

indicators.note: with right sent away, the letter standing for right is dropped

blocks.note: O is the standard abbreviation for old
the Kray twins were notorious London gangsters of the 1960s
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: Someone agrees to the demands of veteran criminals without delay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Right away' looks like 'immediately', but it tells you to remove R from the KRAYS, the Kray brothers who ran organised crime in London's East End.
explanation.definitionFit: To okay something is to approve it, so okays is a verb meaning gives approval or agrees.

clue.text: Drunk cheering, swallowing whiskey in London borough

indicators.note: something drunk is in a muddled state, so these letters are scrambled
swallowing takes something inside, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: taken as written, for rearranging
whiskey is W in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Tipsy revellers knock back whisky in a part of London.
explanation.definitionFit: Greenwich is a borough of south-east London, home of the Royal Observatory and the meridian.

clue.text: Babybel cheddar sandwiches produced burps

indicators.note: a sandwich holds its filling between two outer pieces, so the letters sit inside the phrase

blocks.note: the letters run across the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: Eating cheese sandwiches made someone burp.
explanation.walkthrough: Babybel is a brand of small wax-coated cheese; 'sandwiches' looks like food but is the verb signalling the hidden word.
explanation.definitionFit: To belch is to burp, so belched is the past tense meaning produced burps.

clue.text: Tax demand ultimately deleted

indicators.note: ultimately points to what comes at the end, so only the final letter is kept

blocks.note: excise is a duty or tax on goods
the final letter of demand

explanation.surface: A demand for payment of tax is finally cancelled.
explanation.definitionFit: To excise is to cut out or remove, so excised means deleted or struck out.

clue.text: Great man worked alongside tense overbearing woman

indicators.note: worked means shaped or kneaded, so the letters are reworked into new order

blocks.note: taken as written, for rearranging
T is the grammatical abbreviation for tense

explanation.surface: An important man laboured beside a nervy, domineering woman.
explanation.definitionFit: A termagant is a harsh, quarrelsome and bossy woman, a shrew.

clue.text: Worship always in French church under review primarily

indicators.note: primarily means first of all, so only the opening letter is kept
in a down answer, under places the earlier pieces below the next

blocks.note: the first letter of review
ever means always, as in forever
en is French for in
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: Constant devotion in a French church comes under scrutiny.
explanation.definitionFit: Reverence is deep respect or awe, the attitude of worship towards something holy.

clue.text: Tips American resort to need money being raised

indicators.note: in a down answer, raised means lifted so the word reads upwards

blocks.note: A is the abbreviation for American
a spa is a resort town with mineral springs
sugar is slang for money

explanation.surface: An American holiday town is short of cash, so it raises its prices.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tips' looks like advice or gratuities, but it is the green spears of a vegetable, eaten for their tips.
explanation.definitionFit: Asparagus is eaten mainly for its tender shoots, called tips, so the vegetable is defined by them.

clue.text: Following large bone diners at last clean teeth

indicators.note: at last points to the end of the word, so only its final letter is kept

blocks.note: F is the abbreviation for following, as in page references
L is the abbreviation for large
os is the Latin and anatomical word for bone
the final letter of diners

explanation.surface: After a big bone, the diners finally get to clean their teeth.
explanation.definitionFit: To floss is to clean between the teeth with thread, so the verb matches clean teeth.

clue.text: Texan shows indecision in footwear choice

blocks.note: first meaning: a person keeps reversing a position, as a Texan politician might
second meaning: rubber sandals held by a thong between the toes

explanation.surface: A Texan dithers over which shoes to wear.
explanation.definitionFit: To flip-flop is to keep changing one's mind, and flip-flops are cheap open sandals.

clue.text: Turn to celebrity making comeback

indicators.note: a comeback is a return, so the pieces are read in the opposite direction

blocks.note: taken as written
a VIP is a very important person, a celebrity

explanation.surface: Attention turns to a famous star returning to the limelight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' looks like a link word between definition and wordplay, but it is part of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: To pivot is to turn on a central point, so the verb matches turn.

clue.text: Both parents purchasing oddly neat headgear

indicators.note: oddly keeps the letters in odd-numbered positions
purchasing in its old sense of taking hold, so the parents grip something between them

blocks.note: pa and ma, father and mother
the first and third letters of neat

explanation.surface: Mum and Dad buy a smart hat.
explanation.definitionFit: A Panama is a lightweight woven straw hat, originally made in Ecuador.

clue.text: Fruit Jimmy peeled for each child around

indicators.note: peeling removes the skin, so the outer letters go and the inside is kept
around means one piece is placed so it surrounds the other

blocks.note: per means for each, as in per person
a son is a male child
Jimmy with its first and last letters stripped

explanation.surface: Jimmy peels some fruit for every child nearby.
explanation.definitionFit: The persimmon is an orange fruit from a tree of the ebony family, popular in East Asia.

clue.text: Plant bug

blocks.note: first meaning: a stinging weed
second meaning: to irritate or annoy

explanation.walkthrough: 'Plant bug' suggests a garden pest insect, but bug is a verb here.
explanation.definitionFit: The stinging weed shares its name with the verb meaning irritate or provoke someone.

clue.text: Knew essentially Republican contender is more anxious

indicators.note: the essence of a word lies at its core, so only its central letters are kept

blocks.note: the two central letters of knew
R is the abbreviation for Republican
one who vies, a competitor

explanation.surface: Someone sensed that a Republican rival was getting jumpier.
explanation.walkthrough: VIER is a crossword-friendly word for someone who vies, built from the verb vie.
explanation.definitionFit: Nervier is the comparative of nervy, which means jittery or on edge.

clue.text: Religion Dennis lambasts to some extent

indicators.note: to some extent means only partly, so just part of the phrase is used

blocks.note: the letters run across the end of the first word and into the second

explanation.surface: A man named Dennis partly criticises a faith.
explanation.definitionFit: Islam is the monotheistic faith founded through the Prophet Muhammad.

clue.text: Invalid ultimately had shocking treatment, without entertainment

indicators.note: ultimately points to the very end, so only the last letter is kept
without in its old sense of outside, so one piece wraps around another

blocks.note: the final letter of had
ECT is electroconvulsive therapy, an electric-shock treatment
fun is amusement or entertainment

explanation.surface: A sick patient was finally given harsh therapy with no amusement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Invalid' looks like a noun for a sick person, but it is the adjective meaning void.
explanation.definitionFit: Something defunct no longer exists or operates, so it is invalid or no longer in force.

clue.text: Live prosperously, supporting daughter

indicators.note: in a down answer, a supporting piece sits beneath what it holds up

blocks.note: D is the abbreviation for daughter
to live well is to live prosperously

explanation.surface: Living comfortably while providing for a daughter.
explanation.definitionFit: To dwell is to reside somewhere, so it means live in the sense of having a home.

clue.text: Sound of hooter I will interrupt

indicators.note: to interrupt is to break into, so one piece goes into the middle of the other

blocks.note: hooter is British slang for nose
taken as written

explanation.surface: The car horn's sound will cut in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sound of hooter' suggests a horn's blast; hooter is also British slang for the nose.
explanation.definitionFit: Noise is any sound, especially a loud or unwanted one.

clue.text: Gloom one spread about university speech

indicators.note: spreading things scatters them, so these letters are laid out in new order
about means going round, so the scrambled letters surround one more piece

blocks.note: taken as written, for rearranging
U is the abbreviation for university

explanation.surface: One person's gloom spread across campus.
explanation.definitionFit: A monologue is a long speech by one speaker, as in a play.

clue.text: Alternative that is left for Oxford college

blocks.note: or introduces an alternative
i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, Latin for that is
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: Someone abandoned another option in favour of studying at Oxford.
explanation.definitionFit: Oriel is one of the colleges of the University of Oxford, founded in 1326.

clue.text: This author wears that lady's luxury fashion brand

indicators.note: something worn goes on the outside, so one piece is draped around the other

blocks.note: hers means belonging to that woman
the setter referring to themselves

explanation.surface: The writer is dressed in a woman's designer label.
explanation.walkthrough: 'This author' is the setter, so it gives ME; 'wears' makes HERS the outer piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Hermès is a French luxury house known for silk scarves and Birkin handbags.

clue.text: Follow advice and cook lentils, removing lid

indicators.note: a lid sits on top, so taking it off drops the opening letter
cooking transforms ingredients, so these letters are mixed into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written, before trimming and rearranging

explanation.surface: Do as you are told and prepare the lentils with the pan uncovered.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down-to-earth kitchen surface, 'lid' is the pot's cover; here it is the first letter of the word.
explanation.definitionFit: To listen can mean to heed or take notice, so it works as taking counsel offered.
